title: Source Maps and Production Diagnostics knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is a sound performance or deployment practice?
options: Measure a baseline, run type checks/tests/builds, inspect runtime metrics, and prepare rollback/diagnostic controls.
Assume native compiler speedups guarantee faster application runtime.
Publish source maps and secrets indiscriminately.
questions.answer_key: Measure a baseline, run type checks/tests/builds, inspect runtime metrics, and prepare rollback/diagnostic controls.
questions.explanation: Compiler performance, application runtime performance and deployment reliability are different concerns.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Source Maps and Production Diagnostics”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with source-map configuration and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with source-map configuration and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Source-map configuration”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Source Maps and Production Diagnostics”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check error monitoring, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume managing debugging information safely is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check error monitoring, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Error monitoring”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
